implied subject of 'stretch out', the command in the words Moses is to say to Aaron

links.why: commands joined by waw at one level are one imperative group; the waw is a plain and inside it
'the LORD said to Moses' introduces the command to say to Aaron
'say to Aaron' introduces a collection of commands (stretch out, bring up)

groups.why: the quoted message is the LORD's words, so its sender is the LORD and not Moses (the builder had cl1s); the frame moves to the commanded turn
'stretch out' and 'bring up' are commands joined by and at one level: one imperative group with two command members (cl3 was a part)
Moses is commanded to tell Aaron, so the words he speaks are his (R2), addressed to Aaron, with the quoted LORD message as its part.

none_fit.what: a command that is also the frame of the commanded turn; the imperative kind does not take it as a command member
A relayed message has two turns sharing one saying clause (cl1). Nothing in link_types or group_kinds says a turn carries a message that a messenger was told to deliver, beyond the frame reused.
